articles.title: TechCrunch Mobility: The hidden human cost of robotaxis | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
articles.body_text: Proponents of autonomous vehicle technology have long argued that robotaxis and other self-driving vehicles will reduce crash incidents and make roads safer. And there is some evidence of that. But that doesn’t mean there hasn’t been a cost to those who are working (or have worked) for the companies developing that tech. Sean O’Kane, senior reporter, special projects, dug into data submitted to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration and found that test drivers for Waymo and Zoox sustained more than two dozen injuries in 2024 and 2025 from hard braking or other sudden movements made by the autonomous vehicles. In some cases, these workers were sidelined for months after sustaining injuries like whiplash when the AVs stopped abruptly, and hard. Check out his full story, which includes interviews with former and current workers. There is one important item to consider. You might ask yourself, well what about the other AV developers? Surely, this isn’t a problem isolated to Waymo and Zoox? And you’re probably right. It’s likely that test drivers for other AV developers are also getting injured, but the companies they work for may be exempt from OSHA’s reporting requirements. Got a tip for us on this story or others? Email Kirsten Korosec at kirsten.korosec@techcrunch.com or my Signal at kkorosec.07, Sean O’Kane at sean.okane@techcrunch.com . I’ve been writing about Gatik , the autonomous vehicle startup known for its self-driving box trucks, since 2019 when it came out of “stealth.” At the time, I wasn’t sure if the startup would survive. The hype cycle was already chewing up and spitting out AV startups and no one seemed close to commercializing their tech. Gatik has not only survived, but it has also crossed over from R&D lab to commercial operator, albeit at a small-scale compared with traditional human-driven delivery companies. (The company’s box trucks are driverless and deliver freight from distribution centers to retails stores like Walmart.) And now, with $200 million in fresh funding, it’s pushing to scale. The round was led by Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies, with participation from Millennium Management, ARK Invest, and Intact Private Capital. This is Gatik’s largest funding to date. But I might argue that its multiyear commercial agreement with PepsiCo, which was signed in June and is part of $600 million in contracted revenue, is the bigger deal here. Airbound , an Indian startup building autonomous drones, raised $37 million in a Series A round led by Greenoaks with participation from DoorDash, Lachy Groom, Lightspeed, and Humba Ventures. Mubadala Capital , the alternative asset management arm of Mubadala Investment Company, agreed to acquire a majority equity interest in Arrive Logistics , a truckload brokerage based in Austin. Regent Craft , a Rhode Island electric startup developing and manufacturing electric seagliders, raised $120 million in a Series B round co-led by Mare Liberum and AE Ventures. (The seaglider is a class of vehicle called a wing-in-ground effect vehicle, or WIG.) Regent also secured about $120 million debt capital provided by Erebor Bank, which was launched by Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey. One note about Regent, a company I have followed for a while: The startup, which recently completed its 255,000-square-foot seaglider factory, is clearly pushing deeper into the defense sector, probably because there is money and partnerships to be had. Vista Global Holding , a private aviation group based in UAE, is considering a European IPO that could raise more than a $1 billion, Bloomberg reported.

articles.title: "We're not doing 30 bets a year": Vijay Pande on betting small after running $4 billion at a16z | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Vijay Pande — who left a16z's roughly $4 billion biotech practice last year to start the much smaller, AI-native VZVC — talks about why biology is finally shifting from a "discovery" science to an "engineering" one, why clinical trials are still brutally expensive, and why he thinks open, shared datasets (not walled-off ones) are what will actually let AI transform medicine.
articles.body_text: It used to be that Vijay Pande was better known in academic circles than investor circles. That changed pretty abruptly a dozen years ago, when Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz — who’d spent their firm’s first five years explicitly avoiding healthcare and life sciences — decided the category was worth betting on after all and handed the keys to Pande. At the time, he was a Stanford chemistry professor who was best known for building Folding@home, the distributed-computing project that turned millions of home PCs into a supercomputer for disease research. Over the next decade-plus, he grew a16z’s bet into a practice managing close to $4 billion. So it was somewhat unexpected when in June of last year, Pande walked away from it all to start something much smaller. In fact, his new firm, VZVC , co-founded with longtime investor Zach Werner, is built around a handful of concentrated bets a year rather than dozens, it has no associates, and it relies heavily on AI for its day-to-day operations. To learn more about Pande’s hard pivot, we talked with him this week about why he’s making just a handful of concentrated bets rather than spreading himself thin in the current market — and about one of the more interesting conundrums in AI-driven biotech: unlike text, biological data can’t be scraped off the internet, so nearly every company ends up building its own walled-off dataset. What does that mean for all the advances AI in medicine has promised, and who actually gets access to them? This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. You can also listen to the fuller conversation (below). You’ve said biology is moving from a “science of discovery” to something you can engineer. What does that mean? For a lot of the way drugs have been developed, there was very much a fortuitous aspect to it. I think what’s shifted is that AI and machine learning allow computers to wrap their type of understanding around something very, very complicated… to try to figure out what targets you want your drugs to hit, for specific diseases, to be able to make those drugs, and now even to help in the clinical trials — which are the most expensive part of the process. I thought clinical trials were getting cheaper because drug developers are using more synthetic data, so not as many people are needed for these trials. That’s, I think, very much an aspiration. The cost and time to get to clinical trials has been shrinking, especially with AI, but it could still cost hundreds of millions of dollars to run a trial, which is why drugs are very expensive. The probability of a drug going successfully from the first trial to the end of the third trial is just 20%. If 8 out of 10 fail, and these things cost hundreds of millions of dollars, the amortized cost gets really high. The reason they fail typically is not that the biologist did something wrong; it’s that all the experiments these drugs were designed on were on animal models like mice, and in the end, animal models are just not very predictive of humans. The AI model is not going to be perfect, but it’s going to be way better than any animal model would be, and once it crosses that bar, that’s where it gets really exciting. [The phase after that is]: Is the drug the right drug for me ? The jargon here is so-called precision medicine. If you go to a doctor with something not trivial, they have to guess what’s going on, because there’s only so much they can tell. Then they give you a drug — and if that doesn’t work, they give you another drug, then another drug. This happens in cancer, it happens in lots of different areas. We would all be much better off if the first drug was the right one. Typically, your blood test values are compared to population averages. But really, they should be compared to: is this [result] weird for you? What we’re starting to do also on the medicine side is [the ability] to just understand what would be right for the individual. Would you say the path to this moment has been slow and steady, or did it spike more recently?

articles.title: The Theragun Sense makes everyday recovery surprisingly easy | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The Theragun Sense, which retails for $299, is a wellness-focused massage gun that’s designed for everyday aches, muscle tension, relaxation, and soreness.
articles.body_text: As my 20s are set to come to an end later this year, I’ve officially reached the age where sleeping in the wrong position or stretching just a little too far can cause aches and pains. I’ve always been somewhat skeptical of massage guns, mostly because I’ve tried a few off-brand ones and just assumed they’d eventually end up collecting dust in a drawer. But after a few weeks of testing the Therabody Theragun Sense (2nd Gen) , I was surprised. Turns out massage guns aren’t as gimmicky as I had thought. The Theragun Sense, which retails for $299, is a wellness-focused massage gun that’s designed for everyday aches, muscle tension, relaxation, and soreness. It’s more of a gentle massaging and relaxation tool rather than a hardcore recovery massage gun. If you’re looking for more of a deep-tissue massage, it might be worth checking out the Theragun PRO or Prime. But if you don’t need a super heavy-duty massage gun with features like heated therapy and deep- tissue capabilities, the Theragun Sense is a great option for everyday use. My favorite thing about the massage gun is that it features built-in visually guided routines. The device comes with four routines, and you can access additional routines through the Therabody app and sync your favorite ones to the device using Bluetooth. The Theragun Sense has an LCD screen that walks you through routines step by step. Once you select a routine, the screen shows you exactly where to use the massage gun, how long to spend on each area, and how much pressure to apply. As someone who never really had an idea of what to do with a massage gun other than pointing it to a sore muscle and hoping for the best, I liked that the Therabody Sense takes a lot of the guesswork out of using a massage gun. My favorite routine was the six-minute “Sleep” routine that’s essentially a quick full-body massage to get you ready for the night. The app lets you choose from many other routines, like “Pre-Walk Warm-up,” “Desk Relief,” “Lower Back Recovery,” and more. The massage gun features five speeds to fine-tune pressure to allow for a more relaxing touch, moderate pressure, or a deeper tension release. I liked having the flexibility to change the intensity depending on how sore I was feeling that day. Since the device is designed to be lightweight, I found it easy to hold and get to those spots on my back and shoulders that are harder to reach. For people who want more personalization, the Therabody app takes the guided experience a step further with Coach, the company’s AI feature that creates personalized recovery recommendations based on your goals and activity. Coach can recommend which part of your body to target, which settings or attachments to use, and when to fit a recovery session into your day. The relatively quiet motor was another feature I appreciated, as I could easily use the device while watching TV or relaxing without the sound of the massage gun acting as a distraction.

articles.title: Nvidia’s AI advantage is moving beyond the GPU | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new generation of data center systems is increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles.
articles.body_text: Before this week, the dominant story about Nvidia went something like this: For the first few years of the AI boom, Nvidia was the only source for state-of-the-art GPUs, which became immensely profitable as the industry scaled out. In the last few years, hyperscalers like Amazon and Google have started building their own chips, and Nvidia is no longer the only game in town, leading many investors to wonder how durable its advantage really is. It’s a compelling story, and mostly true. After growing its market cap 10x between the start of 2023 and mid-2025, Nvidia shares have been on a more modest trajectory for the past year, driven by concerns about GPU competition. A new narrative has taken shape since the company’s earnings on Wednesday and investors are starting to realize that Nvidia’s advantage goes far beyond GPUs. As AI’s compute grows into the gigawatt scale, orchestration has become an increasingly complex task. Not surprisingly, Nvidia has built much of the state-of-the-art hardware needed to handle it, giving the company a huge advantage in the systems that surround the GPU even as it sees increased competition on the GPUs themselves. For all the talk of compute as a commodity , it’s still incredibly difficult to operate a megascale data center at peak efficiency — and as deployments get bigger and faster, that challenge is only growing. You can see some of this just by looking at the details of what Nvidia is actually selling. The company is currently rolling out its Vera Rubin architecture, which pairs the Rubin GPU with a collection of other units, including the Vera CPU, the Groq 3 LPX inference accelerator and similar racks for storage and networking. Over the past week, I’ve been talking to folks at Nvidia about what those systems actually do, and the results have been surprising. Like the Rubin GPU itself, they’re extremely specialized systems, but instead of churning through tokens, they’re making sure everything outside the GPU works as efficiently as possible. If the GPU is the engine, these are the rest of the car. The Vera CPU in particular is focused on the problem of orchestrating data. “Vera is important because there’s only so much memory that you can put in a single server or any sort of compute platform,” Jason Hardy, Nvidia’s VP of storage technology, told me. As data centers have scaled up computing power, memory capacity has scaled up too, which is why companies like Micron have gotten rich in the second wave of the infrastructure boom. But getting that data to the GPU at the right time isn’t straightforward — and as companies look to drive tokens-per-watt lower and lower, they’re realizing how important that kind of traffic direction is. “We saw upwards of 3x improvement in these operations, where the Vera CPU is allowing for acceleration,” Hardy said. “So now we can use our flash to its fullest potential, because we can get all that performance out of it without bottlenecking.” You can see versions of the same problem outside of Nvidia. When OpenAI developed its Jalapeño chip, a major focus was avoiding these challenges entirely by minimizing the amount of data that needs to be moved around. “We designed Jalapeño to minimize data movement and communication delays,” the company said in a blog post earlier this month . “Its large domain allows the entire workload to remain within one connected system, minimizing data movement and helping the complete request stay fast and efficient from beginning to end.” It’s a different approach, avoiding data movement entirely by conducting a workload within one integrated chip. But the overall logic is the same, increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles. That in turn opens up a whole new layer of infrastructure for companies to compete over.

articles.title: Chinese automakers are following Tesla’s bet that robots are the next big profit machine | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Technical progress has encouraged a new batch of companies to jump in on the promise of profits from humanoid robots. And they're all Chinese automakers.
articles.body_text: The hype around humanoid robots isn’t particularly new. Thank Tesla CEO Elon Musk and his Optimus robot, as well as the myriad videos of Boston Dynamics’ Atlas robot, for that. Behind that hype, though, there is real progress. The physical capabilities of robots continue to improve, and researchers now believe that the AI techniques behind large language models can make complex robots capable of learning nearly any task. Those tailwinds have encouraged a new batch of companies to jump in on the promise of profits from humanoid robots. And many of the latest entrants are Chinese automakers. Earlier this week, Xpeng’s robotics unit raised more than $900 million at a post-money valuation of more than $6.3 billion. The round, led by IDG Capital with participation from Gaorong Ventures, Tencent, and Alibaba, was described by the company as the largest single-round private financing ever recorded in China’s “embodied AI” industry (AI systems built directly into physical machines). This month, AiMOGA, the robotics unit of China’s Chery Automobile, reportedly began preparing for an IPO , while BYD unveiled a humanoid robot called Xiao Di. Other Chinese automakers, including Changan, GAC, Li Auto, SAIC, and Seres, are also developing humanoid robots. Among all of them, Xpeng is the Chinese automaker that most closely watches and follows Tesla’s initiatives, according to Michael Dunne, CEO of San Diego- and Singapore-based advisory firm Dunne Insights. “It’s the most focused on autonomy, it’s the first to commit in a big way to humanoid robots,” Dunne told TechCrunch, adding that Xpeng founder He Xiaopeng is a tech billionaire known for his agility and quick adjustments. “He sees razor-thin profit in cars on the near horizon. Robots look much more promising.” Xiaopeng and Xpeng co-president Brian Gu are bullish enough that they’ve put their own funds behind the robotics unit. According to the Wall Street Journal , the pair invested about $100 million into the recent fundraising round. Xpeng’s bet is on Iron, a humanoid robot with a realistic human shape that is built for commercial deployment. Chinese automakers like Xpeng do bring a manufacturing edge. “They have all the hardware to get the job done,” Dunne said. “Question is if they can catch Tesla on the AI side of the equation.” There are, of course, many other companies developing humanoid robots, including Agility Robotics, Apptronik , and Figure, all chasing the same goal: commercial deployment at scale.

articles.title: LG buys Homey in a very Samsung SmartThings move
articles.summary: LG has acquired an 80 percent stake in Athom, best known for its Homey smart home platform, in a deal that could help LG compete with Samsung’s SmartThings.
articles.body_text: LG has acquired an 80 percent stake in Athom, a Dutch company best known for its Homey smart home platform. The deal, which LG says will see it acquire the remaining 20 percent of Athom within the next three years, has been forged to expand LG’s smart home ecosystem and should position it to better compete against Samsung’s rivaling SmartThings platform. LG plans to integrate Athom’s existing Homey connectivity — which supports smart devices from Sonos, Ikea, Aqara, Philips Hue, and more — across its appliances through its ThinQ smart home platform. According to Homey, its users will soon be able to control ThinQ-enabled LG appliances via the platform. Homey has developed a significant user base since it was founded in 2014, with its flagship Homey Pro smart home hub capable of connecting to over 50,000 devices across Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Z-Wave, Matter, and Thread. The deal will enable LG to incorporate third-party devices and services into its ThinQ ecosystem for the first time. LG executive vice president Jung Ki-hyun refers to the Athom acquisition as “a cornerstone for our AI home business.” LG announced plans during CES in January to bring so-called “Affectionate Intelligence” to its ThinQ smart home platform — which Homey’s connection to appliances, sensors, and lighting may now play a part in. LG says that Athom will continue to operate as an independent company following the acquisition, retaining its current branding and operations. It’s a similar move to Samsung acquiring SmartThings for $200 million in 2014, which has since seen Samsung building multi-connectivity SmartThings support into soundbars, TVs, smart fridges, monitors, and more. “Homey will continue as it is, with Athom remaining committed to developing Homey Cloud and Homey Pro, and keep working on an ever-expanding lineup of new products,” said Homey in its acquisition statement. “Both the founders, Emile Nijssen & Stefan Witkamp, will stay on as executives of Athom, and continue to execute their vision and create a better smart home for everyone.” The value of the deal has not been officially disclosed, though The Korea Economic Daily reports that it’s estimated to be around 85 billion won ($61 million). LG also hasn’t clarified how Homey’s connectivity and integrations will be embedded into its products but notes that the deal will allow it to “gain deeper insights into customers’ lifestyle and usage patterns” — which may not mesh well with Homey’s “privacy first” ethos.

articles.title: EA is making a single-player Iron Man game
articles.summary: EA is teaming up with Marvel to make a new single-player Iron Man game. The game is currently in development at Motive Studio, which is working on the upcoming Dead Space remake.
articles.body_text: EA is teaming up with Marvel to make a new single-player Iron Man game, EA announced on Tuesday. The game is being developed by Motive Studio, which is working on the upcoming Dead Space remake. EA is describing this new Iron Man title as an “all-new single-player, third-person, action-adventure” Iron Man video game that will feature an “an original narrative that taps into the rich history of Iron Man, channeling the complexity, charisma, and creative genius of Tony Stark, and enabling players to feel what it’s like to truly play as Iron Man.” The new game is currently in preproduction, so it seems as if it could be quite a while before we’ll actually be able to play it. The development team is led by Olivier Proulx, who worked on Square Enix’s well-received Guardians of the Galaxy game from last year. This Iron Man title is just one of many Marvel video games currently in the works, including a currently unnamed game starring Black Panther and Captain America, the card battler Marvel Snap, and the strategy game Midnight Suns from the developers of X-COM. Disney showed glimpses of all those games and more at its recent games showcase. And in Tuesday’s blog post announcing the new Iron Man game, EA teased that it has “several new” Marvel games in development.

A lawyer used ChatGPT and now has to answer for its ‘bogus’ citations
articles.summary: Lawyers representing Roberto Mata in a lawsuit against Avianca submitted a brief citing six cases that don’t exist. Called on the “bogus” citations, a lawyer said they used ChatGPT for research, and it said the cases are real.
articles.body_text: Lawyers suing the Colombian airline Avianca submitted a brief full of previous cases that were just made up by ChatGPT, The New York Times reported today. After opposing counsel pointed out the nonexistent cases, US District Judge Kevin Castel confirmed, “Six of the submitted cases appear to be bogus judicial decisions with bogus quotes and bogus internal citations,” and set up a hearing as he considers sanctions for the plaintiff’s lawyers. Lawyer Steven A. Schwartz admitted in an affidavit that he had used OpenAI’s chatbot for his research. To verify the cases, he did the only reasonable thing: he asked the chatbot if it was lying. [Image: This case isn’t going very well. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24687168/is_varghese_a_real_case.png?quality=90&strip=all] When he asked for a source, ChatGPT went on to apologize for earlier confusion and insisted the case was real, saying it could be found on Westlaw and LexisNexis. Satisfied, he asked if the other cases were fake, and ChatGPT maintained they were all real. The opposing counsel made the court aware of the issue in painful detail as it recounted how the Levidow, Levidow & Oberman lawyers’ submission was a brief full of lies. In one example, a nonexistent case called Varghese v. China Southern Airlines Co., Ltd., the chatbot appeared to reference another real case, Zicherman v. Korean Air Lines Co., Ltd., but got the date (and other details) wrong, saying it was decided 12 years after its original 1996 decision. Schwartz says he was “unaware of the possibility that its content could be false.” He now “greatly regrets having utilized generative artificial intelligence to supplement the legal research performed herein and will never do so in the future without absolute verification of its authenticity.” Schwartz isn’t admitted to practice in the Southern District of New York but originally filed the lawsuit before it was moved to that court and says he continued to work on it. Another attorney at the same firm, Peter LoDuca, became the attorney of record on the case, and he will have to appear in front of the judge to explain just what happened. This once again highlights the absurdity of using chatbots for research without double (or triple) checking their sources somewhere else. Microsoft’s Bing debut is now infamously associated with bald-faced lies, gaslighting, and emotional manipulation. Bard, Google’s AI chatbot, made up a fact about the James Webb Space Telescope in its first demo. Bing even lied about Bard being shut down in a hilariously catty example from this past March. Being great at mimicking the patterns of written language to maintain an air of unwavering confidence isn’t worth much if you can’t even figure out how many times the letter ‘e’ shows up in ketchup. articles.title: Byter namn på sjö
articles.summary: Lake Ontario går inte längre att hitta på amerikanska Google Maps. Nu har sökjätten följt Trumps önskan att byta namn på den ikoniska sjön – till Lake America.
articles.body_text: Lake Ontario går inte längre att hitta på amerikanska Google Maps. Nu har sökjätten gått med på Trumps order att byta namn på den ikoniska sjön – till Lake America. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Ett bittert handelskrig mellan Kanada och USA bröt ut i förra veckan. Länderna har belagt varandra med höga tullsatser och relationen dem sinsemellan har surnat till rejält. Som ett tecken på det fattade USA:s president Donald Trump i torsdags ett beslut om att döpa om sjön Lake Ontario till Lake America, trots att den ligger både i Kanada och USA. – Kanada har under en lång tid blåst oss när det kommer till handel. De betalar inte för någonting och de vill behandlas som en (amerikansk) delstat, men de är inte en delstat, sa Trump i samband med att han skrev under den exekutiva presidentordern. Några dygn senare har även Google ändrat namn på jättesjön, rapporterar CNN. Användare av Googles karttjänst Google Maps i USA kommer inte längre kunna hitta Lake Ontario om man söker på den – i stället står det Lake America. ”Eftersom vi uppdaterar Google Maps för att återspegla namnändringar från officiella myndighetskällor så kommer Maps-användare i USA se 'Lake America'”, skriver Google i ett uttalande. Det innebär att kanadensiska användare fortfarande kommer se sjön som Lake Ontario, eftersom myndigheterna i Kanada inte vill ändra namnet. Trumpadministrationen är till synes nöjd med Googles förändring. Vita husets kommunikationschef Steven Cheung har lagt upp en bild på det nya namnet på X, och Donald Trump själv har länkat till en artikel som handlar om ändringen. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.body_text: Moderaterna vill att polisen enklare ska kunna ingripa mot personer som beter sig hotfullt, skriver TT. – Det räcker med stökiga kaosgrabbar som tror de äger våra gator, säger MUF:s ordförande Douglas Thor. Vallöftet innebär att det nuvarande tillträdesförbudet skulle utvidgas till att polisen får fler möjligheter att gripa in mot personer som beter sig hotfullt ute på gator och torg. Enligt justitieminister Gunnar Strömmer (M) handlar det om att komma åt ett ”antisocialt beteende” när man skulle strama åt den redan befintliga ordningslagen. Den innebär att polisen i nuläget har befogenhet att skicka i väg ordningsstörande personer. Det nya förslaget skulle bland annat innebära att polisen kan utfärda områdesförbud i 30 dagar, men detaljerna i vallöftet är inte helt klara än. Douglas Thor, ordförande för Moderaternas ungdomsförbund, anser att man ”tar tillbaka gatorna” i och med förslaget. – Det räcker med stökiga kaosgrabbar som tror de äger våra gator. Beter de sig inte ska de bort. Vi tar nu ytterligare ett steg för det svenska samhället ska vara enkelt och trevligt för de som gör rätt för sig, och svårt och tufft för de som stör och förstör för andra, säger han i en kommentar till Expressen. articles.title: Katastrof i Grand Canyon – en död
articles.summary: En våldsam översvämning har drabbat Grand Canyon i Arizona. Minst en person är död och 15 saknas. 62 personer har kunnat räddas från katastrofområdet.
articles.body_text: En våldsam översvämning har drabbat Grand Canyon i Arizona. 62 personer har kunnat räddas från katastrofområdet. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Den våldsamma översvämningen började när flera oväder drog in över nationalparken Grand Canyon i lördags. Vattenmassor forsade fram i Bright Angel Canyon och i området kring det historiska hotellet Phantom Ranch, uppger nationalparken . ”Översvämningen orsakade omfattande skador på infrastrukturen i hela Bright Angel Canyon. Nästan alla gångbroar över Bright Angel Creek förstördes, vilket gör att vandrare inte längre kan ta sig över vattnet” , skriver parken i ett uttalande. Under söndagen har luftburna evakueringar skett av åtminstone 62 personer i området – och insatsen fortsätter. Minst 15 personer saknas, rapporterar NBC . Tidigare uppskattade myndigheterna att 20 personer saknades, men den siffran har skrivits ner. En person, en 46-årig man, har hittats omkommen. Han hittades i närheten av forsen Crystal Rapids längs Coloradofloden, skriver CNN. Parken uppmanar alla som känner till vandrare eller backpackers som befann sig i området eller som hade planerat att ta sig till det drabbade området att kontakta myndigheterna så snart som möjligt. Översvämningen har även slagit ut en vattenledning, vilket försvårar situationen ytterligare. Den förstörda vattenledningen förser alla anläggningar i South Rim – den största och mest besökta delen av hela Grand Canyon – med dricksvatten och vatten för brandsläckning. ”Ett stort antal campingplatser och vandringsleder är stängda tills vidare. Det finns ingen prognos för när de drabbade områdena kan öppna igen” , skriver nationalparken. Platsen där översvämningarna har inträffat ligger avskilt, och är inte tillgängligt att nå med bil. Grand Canyon är ett mycket populärt resmål i USA. Över 4 miljoner turister besöker parken varje år.

articles.title: Trump kräver: Straffa henne – hur kan hon?
articles.summary: Donald Trump hotar journalisten Kristen Welker med bestraffning. Och säger att ”något måste göras” åt ”falska” opinionsmätningar. Till sin hjälp vill han återigen ta tillsynsmyndigheten FCC.
articles.body_text: Donald Trump hotar journalisten Kristen Welker med bestraffning. Och säger att ”något måste göras” åt ”falska” opinionsmätningar. Till sin hjälp vill han återigen ta tillsynsmyndigheten FCC. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Donald Trump säger att journalisten Kristen Welker bör ”bestraffas” av FCC. Han kräver också att myndigheten agerar mot det han kallar falska opinionsmätningar i medierna. FCC har egentligen inte rätt att straffa journalister eller stoppa åsikter i sändningar. Donald Trump viftar återigen vilt mot pressfriheten. I två inlägg kort efter varandra ger han order till FCC, myndigheten som bland annat ansvarar för sändningstillstånd i USA, att stoppa inslag och personer med budskap han inte gillar. Först slog han fast att han kommer att ”rapportera” Kristen Welker, programledare för NBC News ”Meet the Press”, till FCC så att hon kan ”tillrättavisas eller bestraffas” på grund av att hon avsiktligt skulle sprida felaktigheter. I det andra skrev han att de ”falska opinionsmätningar som våra korrupta medier använder har spårat ur fullständigt” och lade till ”FCC till undsättning!” Inlägget kom efter ett inslag i en annan tv-kanal där Kristen Welker, som gäst, sagt att Trumps inflytande över mellanårsvalet kommer att bli stort. – Han har gett sitt stöd till en rad kandidater i primärvalen. Resultaten har varit blandade, sa Welker. Att hon direkt nämnde Darline Graham, den nyligen avlidna Lindsey Grahams syster, som ett exempel där Trumps kandidat vunnit hjälpte inte mot presidentens ilska. Han attackerar henne för att vara en ”impopulär värdinna”, kallar programmet för ”Meet the Fake Press” och skriver att hans kandidater vunnit nästan samtliga primärval.

articles.title: Vill ha en ursäkt – är lika arg som tidigare
articles.summary: Prins Harry har återvänt till Storbritannien med Meghan. Men han är fortfarande lika ilsken. – Han förväntar sig fortfarande en ursäkt, säger en vän enligt Daily Mail.
articles.body_text: Prins Harry har återvänt till Storbritannien med Meghan. – Han förväntar sig fortfarande en ursäkt, säger en vän enligt Daily Mail . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Prins Harry uppges fortfarande vara arg på delar av kungafamiljen och väntar fortfarande på en ursäkt. Vänner som träffat honom igen blev förvånade, enligt Daily Mail. De hade väntat sig en mer ödmjuk ton. Samtidigt kräver Harry starkare säkerhet för sig och sin familj, enligt The Times. Prins Harry och hertiginnan Meghan lämnade Storbritannien i ilska för sex år sedan. När de kom tillbaka tillsammans med sina två barn, Archie, 7, och Lilibet, 5, för någon vecka sedan trodde många att ilskan hade lagt sig. Men enligt källor till Daily Mail är de fortfarande lika arga. – Vänner som träffade Harry igen väntade sig att få höra en mer ångerfull och ödmjuk ton, säger en vän. Men i stället är det snarare tvärtom – han är fortfarande i ”Oprah-läge”, som källan uttrycker det och syftar på den ökända intervjun då Harry och Meghan bland annat talade om att någon i kungafamiljen, utan att nämna namn, var orolig för hur mörk hy deras då ofödda son skulle få. – De häpnade över att höra att han fortfarande känner ilska mot medlemmar av kungafamiljen, fortfarande är frustrerad över 'männen i grå kostymer' som omger hans far, och fortfarande väntar sig en ursäkt, fortsätter källan. Harry har vid upprepade tillfällen anklagat ”män i grå kostymer” – medarbetare vid hovet – för att försöka sabotera hans försoning med kung Charles.

articles.title: Trumps hot: ”Sprängs i småbitar!!!”
articles.summary: Strider blossar upp igen i Mellanöstern. USA har bombat en ö i Hormuzsundet – och hotar att spränga nästa i ”småbitar”. Iran svarar med ballistiska robotar mot Jordanien.
articles.body_text: Strider blossar upp igen i Mellanöstern. USA har bombat en ö i Hormuzsundet – och hotar att spränga nästa i ”småbitar”. Iran svarar med ballistiska robotar mot Jordanien. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det blev en dryg månad av relativt lugn i Iran . Natten mot måndagen har striderna mellan USA och Iran blossat upp igen. För första gången sedan den 29 juli har USA bekräftat ett angrepp mot Iran. Det amerikanska centralkommandot (Centcom), som leder USA:s styrkor i Mellanöstern, bekräftar att de har bombat två iranska raketramper på ön Larak i Hormuzsundet. Enligt kommandot höll ramperna på att förbereda avfyrning av raketer laddade med sjöminor in i sundet när de slogs ut. – Förra veckan avslutade Centcom röjningen av sjöminor från sundets internationella farleder. Vi kommer inte att tillåta Iran att lägga ut fler minor, säger Tim Hawkins, kommandots talesperson, enligt Wall Street Journal. Under tidig måndagsmorgon hotar Trump även med att spränga den viktiga ön Kharg som är Irans viktigaste oljeexportshamn i ”småbitar”. I ett inlägg på Truth Social har han publicerat en AI-producerad video som föreställer att ön attackeras från luften. ”Kharg Island sprängs i småbitar!!!”, skriver presidenten i inlägget. Irans revolutionsgarde uppger att flera soldater och civila dödades och skadades i de amerikanska attackerna på den strategiskt belägna ön, varifrån Iran övervakar och kontrollerar trafiken genom sundet. Kort därpå avfyrade Iran ballistiska robotar och drönare mot Jordanien, uppger både den amerikanska militären och Irans revolutionsgarde. Enligt amerikanerna har robotarna skjutits ner. Jordanien uppger att åtta robotar har stoppats. Inga skador ska ha uppstått enligt dessa uppgifter, men revolutionsgardet hävdar att robotarna – riktade mot två amerikanska flygbaser – orsakat stora skador. Attackerna gjorde att priset på olja omedelbart steg till över 90 dollar fatet igen.

articles.title: 30-tal döda på äldreboende i Kiev
articles.summary: När ett vapenlager träffades i en rysk attack mot Kiev under fredagen ledde det till stor förödelse. Ett 30-tal personer på ett äldreboende dödades i attacken.
articles.body_text: När ett vapenlager träffades i en rysk attack mot Kiev under fredagen ledde det till stor förödelse. Ett 30-tal personer på ett äldreboende dödades i attacken. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det var i fredagskväll som ett ammunitionslager i byn Myla utanför Kiev träffades i en rysk attack. Minst 38 personer dog i vad som beskrivs som den dödligaste attacken i Ukraina i år, enligt AP. De flesta av dem är boende på ett äldreboende, skriver Ukrainska Pravda . Enligt tidningen har 27 kroppar identifierats. Ett 100-tal bostadshus skadades och över 40 personer skadades, enligt BBC. – Allt är helt förstört, säger Liubov Pavlenko, 45, boende i området till BBC. 370 personer har evakuerats från området. Presidenten Volodymyr Zelenskyj skriver på Telegram att attacken ledde till en explosion på fastigheterna nära ett hem för äldre och funktionsnedsatta. Händelsen kommer att utredas av polis. Det är enligt Zelenskyj inte tillåtet att förvara ammunition i närheten av bostadshus. ”Det finns regler: ammunition får inte finnas i närheten av bostadshus eller annan bostadsbebyggelse. Det kommer definitivt att komma relevanta åtgärder” , skriver han. Tidigare i juli exploderade ett annat ammunitionslager i Vyshneve i en rysk attack.

articles.title: M vill porta hotfulla personer från torgen | Expressen
articles.summary: Den 13 september går Sverige till val. Följ Expressens direktrapport med senaste nytt inför valet.
articles.body_text: Moderaterna vill utvidga tillträdesförbudet till att gälla även personer som agerar allmänt hotfullt på offentliga platser. Moderaterna kallar sitt vallöfte för Trygghetsskapande områdesförbud, där polisen får skärpta möjligheter att ingripa mot personer som uppträder hotfullt på gator och torg. Förslaget kan ses som en förlängning av vistelseförbudet och ordningslagen, enligt justitieminister Gunnar Strömmer. Polisen ska kunna utfärda ett områdesförbud i förslagsvis 30 dagar. Liberalernas partiledare Simona Mohamsson kommenterar meningsutbytet mellan Jimmie Åkesson och Ebba Busch. – Bra att Ebba talar in Jimmie i lagspel, nu är tiden för mål mot vänstern och passningar inom högern. Vi behöver fler angrepp på samhällsproblemen och färre på varandra om vi tillsammans ska stoppa de rödgröna. Jimmie Åkesson kritiserade Ebba Buschs vänsterflört med oppositionen i sitt sommartal under lördagen. Han frågade sig om det verkligen går att lita på Ebba Busch , och tyckte att ”vänsterflörten” var en dålig strategi. – Det är klart att man kan lita på mig, svarade Ebba Busch. Socialdemokraternas rättspolitiska talesperson Teresa Carvalho presenterar flera vallöften om arbetet mot mäns våld mot kvinnor. Reformerna innefattar bland annat höjda straff för grov kvinnofridskränkning och fördubblad prövotid för män som döms för sexualbrott – från två till fyra år. S vill även införa en samlad brottsoffer-lag som ska göra rättigheterna tydliga för den som utsätts. Cavarlho säger också att de vill "stoppa Tidöregeringens massnedläggning av skyddade boenden för kvinnor". – Poängen med de här åtgärderna är i grunden mycket enkel, nämligen att Sverige ska bli ett tryggare land för kvinnor att leva i. Sverige ska bli bäst i Europa på att skydda kvinnor innan våldet sker, säger Teresa Carvalho på pressträffen.
